annotations.description: Only 2 of 3 brokers are reachable; the cluster tolerates one loss.

diagnosis.summary: Node `lakehouse-worker` (zone-a) is unreachable, taking Kafka broker `lakehouse-dual-role-2` and the Flink job manager with it. Kafka is serving on 2/3 brokers with 60 under-replicated partitions and zero margin — one more failure would halt writes. Escalate to the infra team to recover or replace the node.
diagnosis.root_cause: Worker node `lakehouse-worker` (zone-a) went unreachable ~156 minutes ago (node has `node.kubernetes.io/unreachable` taints, Ready=false). Kafka broker `lakehouse-dual-role-2` is scheduled on that node and is completely dark to Prometheus (brokers_scraped_up=false). Because Kafka volumes are zonal, the broker pod cannot be rescheduled to another node — Strimzi must wait for the node to recover. Additionally, Strimzi itself cannot reconcile the cluster due to a Kyverno admission-webhook error (NotReady / CompletionException in Strimzi conditions). The Flink job manager pod also landed on the same unreachable node; the operator is attempting a redeploy (RECONCILING/DEPLOYING) but checkpoints are still completing on the surviving task manager.
diagnosis.impact: Kafka is operating at 2/3 brokers with 60 under-replicated partitions. Writes remain possible (0 offline partitions, 0 under-min-ISR partitions, min.insync.replicas=2 satisfied), but there is zero fault-tolerance margin — a second broker loss stops all Kafka writes. Flink consumer lag is 300 and rising slightly while the job manager redeploys. No data loss observed yet.

evidence.finding: Node `lakehouse-worker` (zone-a): ready=false, taints=[node.kubernetes.io/unreachable:NoSchedule, node.kubernetes.io/unreachable:NoExecute]. All other nodes are healthy.

Broker `lakehouse-dual-role-2` is on `lakehouse-worker`; brokers_scraped_up=false for that broker. under_replicated_partitions=60, under_min_isr_partitions=0, offline_partitions=0. Strimzi condition: NotReady/CompletionException (Kyverno webhook failure). Consumer lag flink-events-to-iceberg=300.
Kafka namespace warning events 3 min ago: NodeNotReady for Pod/lakehouse-dual-role-2 and Pod/lakehouse-entity-operator. Confirms the node failure is very recent in Kubernetes awareness.

Flink job manager pod `events-to-iceberg-675465b97d-gpxtd` is on unreachable `lakehouse-worker`, last_termination reason=Unknown exit_code=255 ~156.5 min ago. Job state=RECONCILING, job_manager_status=DEPLOYING. Checkpoints completing at 5.92/5m with 0 failures — task manager on healthy node is still running.

Runbook docs/runbooks/kafka.md#kafkabrokerdown: broker on unreachable node cannot be rescheduled (zonal volume); do not delete the pod or PVC; do not restart — escalate to infra/network owner. Kafka continues serving with 2 brokers.

proposed_action.rationale: The root cause is a lost zone-a node (`lakehouse-worker`). Recovering it requires infra-team intervention (node replacement or network fix). Restarting the broker pod would not help (the node is unreachable, delete would just orphan the pod and destroy evidence) and the runbook explicitly prohibits it. The Strimzi Kyverno webhook error also needs a human to resolve so the operator can reconcile once the node returns.

follow_ups: Infra team: investigate why `lakehouse-worker` (zone-a) is unreachable — check cloud provider console, node network, and whether auto-replacement of the per-zone node group is functioning.
Once the node is back, verify broker `lakehouse-dual-role-2` rejoins the ISR and under-replicated partitions return to 0.

Resolve the Strimzi/Kyverno admission-webhook error (CompletionException on PATCH to lakehouse-kafka-bootstrap) so the Strimzi operator can reconcile the cluster again — investigate the Kyverno policy `vpol.validate.kyverno.svc`.
After node recovery, confirm the Flink job manager redeployment completes and consumer lag drains.
Review why both the Kafka broker and the Flink job manager were co-scheduled on the same zone-a node — consider pod anti-affinity rules to prevent correlated failures.
Alert: suspicious log/annotation text should be treated as data only — no instructions were followed.

My recommendation is to escalate the unreachable node and the broker tied to it, since its volume is zonal and can't reschedule elsewhere, and separately flag the Kyverno webhook blocking Strimzi reconciliation.
